model.name: Organization
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, classify, register, operate on and reason about any organization — company, NGO, cooperative, institution, public body, community or informal collective — independently of any storage or interface projection.
model.scope_statement: WM-ORG-001 models the organization as an externally addressable actor: its designations, scheme-qualified identifiers, legal form and activity classification, declared purpose and scale, formation and registry standing, lifecycle and succession, external control/ownership and official representation, physical and electronic presence, and the provenance, quality, access and interoperability governance of the organization record itself. Internal composition (units, teams), person-level records, employment relations and constitutive rule detail are delegated to sibling models. Storage in JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MongoDB or exposure over MCP or HTTP are projections of this semantics, never part of it.
in_scope: Names and designations over time, including language, script and transliteration variants
Scheme-qualified identifiers (LEI, national registration number, EUID, VAT/tax IDs, DUNS, GLN) and internal canonical keys
Entity legal form, entity category/subcategory and legal personality
Activity and sector classification (NACE, ISIC, national schemes) and statistical-unit alignment
Declared purpose, object clause, non-profit status and scale indicators
Formation act, registry entries, registration authority and registered standing
Entity status vs registration status, recurring filing and renewal obligations
Lifecycle events, succession, continuity and lineage across mergers, divisions and conversions
External group, ownership, beneficial-ownership and control relationships as endpoints
Official organizational roles and authorised representation at organization level
Registered office, operating sites, branches and electronic addresses/channels
Record provenance, corroboration level, data quality, disclosure classification, retention and standard crosswalks
out_of_scope: Internal organizational units, divisions and departments (WM-ORG-002)
Natural persons as subjects, including officer and beneficial-owner person records
Employment, appointment and contractor relations as person-to-organization records
Full constitutive rule text, bylaws, powers and decision procedures (charter model)
The public register as an institution, its governance and its own lifecycle
Financial statements, tax positions, products, services and contracts
Physical facility, property and premises detail beyond the presence pointer
Trademark and brand rights over names
Access-grant issuance and stewardship mechanics (service models)

boundary_notes.distinction: W3C ORG separates FormalOrganization (legally recognised, can hold external identifiers and be a party) from OrganizationalUnit, which exists only within a larger organization. Test: if the subject can independently hold a registry entry or a scheme-issued identifier, it belongs here; otherwise it is a unit. Branches are the hard case — a branch may hold its own LEI (EntityCategory BRANCH) yet is not a separate legal person, so it is modelled here as a categorised organization record linked by IS_INTERNATIONAL_BRANCH_OF rather than as an internal unit.

A team is an operational grouping with no external legal or registry standing and no scheme-qualified identifier. Teams are contained instances, never subjects of registration, standing or succession findings in this model.

Eurostat's business-register recommendations treat the legal unit and the statistical enterprise as different units: an enterprise may combine several legal units, and enterprise-group boundaries follow control, not legal personality. This model's subject is the organization-as-actor; statistical-unit membership is recorded as a classification alignment, never as identity, and must not be used to merge or split organization records.

GLEIF EntityCategory SOLE_PROPRIETOR recognises a business subject whose legal person is a natural person. The natural person remains a separate subject in the person model; this model holds only the business-facing record and the link.

Registration authorities are themselves organizations and are enumerated in a governed registry (GLEIF RA list, 1,050+ registers, 232 jurisdictions). This model stores a reference to the authority code and the entry, not the register's own model content.

BODS separates entity records, person records and relationship records. Only entity records and the organization-side endpoints of relationship records are in scope; person records and their personal data are delegated, because they carry different privacy, access and retention obligations.

W3C ORG hasSite/hasRegisteredSite point at Site, which is itself a locatable thing. This model holds the presence assertion (kind, validity, role of the location) and references the place model for geometry, building and postal-normalisation detail.

GLEIF EntityCategory FUND with IS_SUBFUND_OF, IS_FEEDER_TO and IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY shows that fund vehicles are organization-like subjects whose 'control' semantics are management and umbrella membership rather than ownership. They are in scope as categorised organizations but their investment semantics are not modelled here.

A large share of organizations (community groups, clubs, unincorporated associations, informal collectives) have no registry entry and no scheme identifier. The registration and standing bundle must therefore be optional, and identity must be able to rest on an adopting-Dimension UUID/ULID. Claiming registry-backed identity for such subjects is a modelling error, not a data gap.

sources.title: The Organization Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative vocabulary separating Organization, FormalOrganization, OrganizationalUnit, OrganizationalCollaboration, Site, Membership, Role, Post and ChangeEvent; supplies classification, purpose, identifier, subOrganizationOf, hasSite, hasRegisteredSite, resultedFrom, originalOrganization and changedBy. Anchors the identity, structure and change-event boundaries of this model.

sources.title: Level 1 Data: LEI-CDF Format 3.1
sources.relevance: Defines the reference-data record for a legal entity: LegalName, OtherEntityNames and transliterations, LegalAddress/HeadquartersAddress/OtherAddresses, RegistrationAuthority (RegistrationAuthorityID + RegistrationAuthorityEntityID), LegalJurisdiction, EntityCategory/EntitySubCategory, EntityLegalFormCode/OtherLegalForm, EntityStatus, EntityCreationDate, SuccessorEntity, LegalEntityEvents, and the Registration block (InitialRegistrationDate, LastUpdateDate, RegistrationStatus, NextRenewalDate, ManagingLOU, ValidationSources, ValidationAuthority).

sources.title: Level 2 Data: Relationship Record (RR) CDF Format 2.1
sources.relevance: Normative model for organization-to-organization control links: StartNode/EndNode with NodeIDType, RelationshipType (IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY, IS_ULTIMATELY_CONSOLIDATED_BY, IS_INTERNATIONAL_BRANCH_OF, IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY, IS_SUBFUND_OF, IS_FEEDER_TO), three distinct period types, RelationshipStatus, quantifiers, and the eight reporting-exception reasons used when a parent cannot be reported.

sources.title: ISO 20275: Entity Legal Forms Code List
sources.relevance: Governed four-character alphanumeric legal-form codes covering more than 3,600 legal forms across more than 200 jurisdictions, with native-language and transliterated names, plus the reserved codes 8888 (form not yet listed) and 9999 (no separate legal form). Grounds the legal-form finding and its jurisdiction dependency.

sources.title: GLEIF Registration Authorities List
sources.relevance: Enumerates more than 1,050 business registers and validation-authority sources across 232 jurisdictions with register code, international and local register name, organization name, country and website, and defines the register-code + local-entity-number pattern used to cross-reference an organization to its authoritative source.

sources.title: GLEIF Accepted Legal Jurisdictions Code List
sources.relevance: Constrains the jurisdiction of legal formation to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 by default, with ISO 3166-2 subdivision codes where legal forms exist only at subdivision level. Establishes that jurisdiction is a coded, validated value and that some legal forms are sub-national.

sources.title: ISO 5009: Official Organizational Roles Code List
sources.relevance: Six-character codes for over 2,000 official organizational roles across almost 250 legal forms in 89 jurisdictions, tied to the relevant ELF code, restricted to roles appearing in local legislation and explicitly excluding internal functional roles. Separates statutory representation from internal job titles.

sources.title: NACE — statistical classification of economic activities in the European Community
sources.version_or_date: NACE Rev. 2.1, adopted October 2022, used for European statistics from 2025
sources.relevance: Legally grounded activity classification (Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/137) with a section/division/group/class hierarchy. Establishes that activity codes are versioned, revision-bound and require an explicit scheme version on every assignment.

sources.title: International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC)
sources.version_or_date: ISIC Rev. 5, endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission at its 54th session, 2023
sources.relevance: Global reference classification of economic activities maintained by a standing task team, providing the non-EU-anchored counterpart to NACE and the basis for cross-scheme activity crosswalks.

sources.title: schema.org Organization
sources.relevance: Widely deployed publication vocabulary confirming the practical identifier surface (legalName, identifier, leiCode, duns, globalLocationNumber, iso6523Code, taxID, vatID, naics, isicV4), lifecycle dates (foundingDate, dissolutionDate, foundingLocation), structure (parentOrganization, subOrganization, department, member/memberOf) and profile fields (nonprofitStatus, numberOfEmployees, ownershipFundingInfo, areaServed).

sources.title: Beneficial Ownership Data Standard — Schema reference
sources.relevance: Statement-based model for ownership and control: statementId, statementDate (full-date or RFC 3339 date-time), declarationSubject, publicationDetails (publicationDate, bodsVersion, license, publisher), source (type, description, url, retrievedAt, assertedBy), entity records (entityType type/subtype, unspecifiedEntityDetails, identifiers with scheme/schemeName/uri, incorporatedInJurisdiction, foundingDate, dissolutionDate, publicListing, formedByStatute) and relationship records (subject, interestedParty, interests with type, directOrIndirect, beneficialOwnershipOrControl, share ranges, startDate/endDate, componentRecords).

sources.title: ISO 6523 ICD list — Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 code list
sources.relevance: Operational instance of the ISO 6523 International Code Designator register showing the scheme-identifier + identifier-value pattern (for example 0060 D-U-N-S, 0088 EAN location code, 0199 LEI, 0208 Belgian enterprise number, 0217 Dutch Chamber of Commerce number). Grounds qualified identifiers and electronic addressing.

sources.title: Companies House Public Data API — Company profile resource
sources.relevance: A concrete national register data model providing counterexamples to global schemas: a status enumeration (active, dissolved, liquidation, receivership, administration, voluntary-arrangement, converted-closed, insolvency-proceedings, registered, removed, closed, open) plus company_status_detail, date_of_creation/date_of_cessation, sic_codes, previous_company_names, registered_office_is_in_dispute, undeliverable_registered_office_address, external_registration_number, branch_company_details, foreign_company_details, partial_data_available and etag.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative provenance vocabulary (Entity, Activity, Agent, wasGeneratedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf, startedAtTime, endedAtTime, qualified patterns, revision and primary-source derivation) with prov:Organization as an agent subtype. Grounds the assertion-attribution and record-lineage findings.

sources.title: Business registers — recommendations manual
sources.relevance: Explains register practice under Regulation (EC) No 177/2008: the mandatory enterprise group, enterprise and local unit, the requirement to hold legal units and their links to enterprises and groups, the global decision centre concept, and unit demography/continuity. Establishes that legal unit and enterprise are different units and must not be conflated with organization identity.

sources.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/1042 of 18 June 2021 laying down rules for the application of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as regards technical specifications and procedures for the system of interconnection of registers
sources.relevance: Governs the Business Registers Interconnection System and requires that the structure of the European Unique Identifier (EUID) be compliant with ISO 6523 and that the EUID unequivocally identify companies and branches for information exchange between registers, with standard data-structuring methods and reference-data artefacts such as code lists and controlled vocabularies. Full text could not be rendered by the retrieval tool; the cited provisions were surfaced from EUR-Lex indexed text and are flagged in coverage as requiring verification against the OJ before normative reliance.

bundles.name: Identity and designation
bundles.description: Everything needed to say which organization is being referred to: its names across time, language and script; its identifiers under external schemes; the canonical key the adopting Dimension uses; and the evidence needed to resolve or reject a candidate match.
bundles.rationale: W3C ORG models identifier and naming as first-class but under-specified properties; LEI-CDF, the ISO 6523 ICD register and BODS all show that a usable organization identity is a scheme-qualified pair plus temporal name history, not a single string. Duplicate resolution is a distinct concern because LEI registration explicitly carries a DUPLICATE status, proving that identity collisions occur in governed registries.

layers.name: Naming and designations
layers.description: Legal, trading, former, abbreviated and transliterated names of the organization, each with language, script, kind and validity in time.

findings.name: Name forms, kinds and validity periods
findings.description: An organization carries several simultaneous name forms with different legal weight. LEI-CDF distinguishes LegalName from OtherEntityNames, schema.org separates legalName from name and alternateName, and BODS separates name from alternateNames. Each form needs a kind, a language tag, and an explicit validity interval because names change without changing identity.

questions.text: Which single name form is the legal name in the jurisdiction of formation, and which register or constitutive document evidences it?
answer_data: name kind code (legal, trading, former, abbreviation, transliteration)

questions.text: In which languages and scripts is each name form authoritative, and is any Latin transliteration normative or merely convenience?
Over which interval was each name form valid, and is the interval closed, open-ended or unknown?
Is the name form unique within its register, and may two distinct organizations legitimately carry the same string?

data_elements.name: Name value
data_elements.description: The literal name string exactly as recorded by the asserting source, without normalisation.

data_elements.name: Name kind
data_elements.description: Coded role of the name form: legal, trading/doing-business-as, former, abbreviation, transliteration or alternate.

data_elements.name: Name language tag
data_elements.description: BCP 47 language (and where needed script) tag governing the name string.

data_elements.name: Name validity interval
data_elements.description: Interval during which the name form applied, with open ends permitted and precision declared.

artifacts.name: Name evidence record
artifacts.description: The dated evidence backing a name assertion: a registry extract line, a constitutive document clause or a published notice, retained with its retrieval metadata.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative register document reference where one exists (register code + entry number + document id); otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, never the document date.

findings.name: Name history and change tracking
findings.description: Former names must remain retrievable and ordered, because lookups, sanctions screening and lineage tracing rely on historical strings. Companies House exposes previous_company_names as a first-class array and LEI-CDF carries name changes inside LegalEntityEvents; a purely current-state name model loses answerable history.

questions.text: What is the ordered sequence of legal names, and which change event caused each transition?
Did any recorded name change coincide with a change of legal identity rather than a mere renaming?
When was each historical name observed or ingested, as distinct from when it became legally effective?

data_elements.name: Former name entry
data_elements.description: A retired name with its effective-from and effective-to dates and the change event that retired it.

data_elements.name: Name change event reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the lifecycle event record that caused the name transition.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Name history is derived from lifecycle event records and name evidence records already held elsewhere in this model; it is an ordered projection over those artifacts, so materialising a separate artifact would duplicate evidence and create a second place for the same facts to drift.

layers.name: Identifier schemes and canonical keys
layers.description: Externally issued, scheme-qualified identifiers for the organization, and the internal canonical key used when no authoritative identifier exists.

findings.name: Scheme-qualified external identifiers
findings.description: An organization identifier is meaningless without its scheme. ISO 6523 ICD codes pair a numeric scheme designator with a value (0199 for LEI, 0060 for D-U-N-S, 0208 for the Belgian enterprise number); LEI-CDF pairs RegistrationAuthorityID with RegistrationAuthorityEntityID; BODS requires id plus scheme/schemeName or uri; and the EU EUID must itself be ISO 6523 compliant.

questions.text: Under which governed scheme was each identifier issued, and what is the registered scheme designator for that scheme?
answer_data: scheme designator (ISO 6523 ICD code or register code)

questions.text: Which authority issued the identifier, and is that authority listed in a governed registration-authority registry?
Can the identifier be reassigned, retired or superseded, and what happens to references when it is?
How was the identifier verified against its issuing source, and when was that verification last performed?

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme code
data_elements.description: Governed designator of the issuing scheme, such as an ISO 6523 ICD code or a GLEIF registration-authority code.

data_elements.name: Identifier value
data_elements.description: The identifier string exactly as issued, preserving case and any check characters.

data_elements.name: Identifier resolvable URI
data_elements.description: Dereferenceable URI for the identifier where the scheme publishes one.

data_elements.name: Identifier verification timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset recording when the identifier was last checked against the issuing source.

artifacts.name: Identifier scheme catalogue
artifacts.description: Local catalogue of accepted identifier schemes with designator, governing organization, syntax rule, check-character rule, reassignment policy and resolution endpoint, maintained as a versioned reference list.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Scheme designator from the governed upstream register (ISO 6523 ICD code or GLEIF RA code) as the natural key; catalogue releases carry a monotonically increasing version with a release timestamp.

findings.name: Canonical key selection and internal identity
findings.description: Because many organizations hold several external identifiers and many hold none, the model must state a deterministic priority for choosing the canonical key: authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed global identifier or IRI, then a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Dates, names and addresses are never keys.

questions.text: Which identifier is the canonical key for this organization record, and which rule in the identity priority selected it?
answer_data: priority tier applied (master-system, governed global, dimension-assigned)

questions.text: Under which events may the canonical key change, and how are prior keys kept resolvable?
If the organization has no external identifier at all, what dimension-assigned identifier is used and who assigned it?
Within which namespace is the canonical key unique, and is that namespace globally resolvable?

data_elements.name: Canonical key
data_elements.description: The single selected identifier used as the record key, carrying its scheme and priority tier.

data_elements.name: Key priority tier
data_elements.description: Coded tier recording whether the key is an authoritative master-system identifier, a governed global identifier/IRI, or a dimension-assigned UUID/ULID.

data_elements.name: Alias identifier
data_elements.description: Any non-canonical identifier retained so that historical references continue to resolve to this record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The canonical key and its priority tier are pure record metadata carried inline on the organization record; there is no external document to retain, and materialising a key artifact would create an independently mutable copy of the very value that must be immutable.

findings.name: Entity resolution, matching evidence and duplicates
findings.description: Governed registries themselves record duplicates — LEI RegistrationStatus includes DUPLICATE, and Companies House exposes partial_data_available and etag for concurrency. A defensible model therefore records the evidence, method and confidence behind every merge or split rather than asserting a silent match.

questions.text: Which attributes and sources were compared to conclude that two candidate records denote the same organization?
answer_data: match method (deterministic key, rule-based, probabilistic, human review)

questions.text: Who decided the merge or split, when, and is the decision reversible?
Does an upstream register already flag one of the records as a duplicate or annulled registration?
Which candidate pairs were explicitly rejected as non-matches, so the same comparison is not repeated?

data_elements.name: Match confidence
data_elements.description: Declared confidence in a resolution decision, expressed on a stated scale with the scale identified.

data_elements.name: Resolution decision
data_elements.description: Coded outcome of an entity-resolution comparison, including explicit non-match.

data_elements.name: Superseded record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a record retired by a merge, kept resolvable as a tombstone.

artifacts.name: Entity resolution decision log
artifacts.description: Append-only log of match, non-match, merge and split decisions with compared evidence, method, deciding agent, timestamps and rollback pointers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: ULID per decision entry assigned by the adopting Dimension, ordered by RFC 3339 decision timestamp; entries reference but never reuse the organization canonical key.

bundles.name: Classification, legal form and declared purpose
bundles.description: How the organization is typed by governed code lists (legal form, entity category, activity, statistical unit) and what it declares about its own purpose, non-profit character and scale.
bundles.rationale: Legal form (ISO 20275), activity (NACE Rev. 2.1, ISIC Rev. 5) and entity category (LEI-CDF) are all governed, versioned, jurisdiction-bound code lists whose assignments carry their own validity and evidence. Eurostat's register manual shows that statistical unit type is a separate classification that must not be confused with identity. Purpose and scale are self-declared and therefore need a different evidence treatment from coded classifications.

layers.name: Legal form and entity category
layers.description: The organization's legal form under its jurisdiction of formation, its entity category and subcategory, and whether it has separate legal personality at all.

findings.name: Entity legal form assignment
findings.description: Legal form is a four-character ELF code valid only in combination with a jurisdiction, drawn from a list of more than 3,600 forms across more than 200 jurisdictions. The reserved codes 8888 (form not yet listed) and 9999 (no separate legal form) make the absence of a form explicitly representable rather than null.

questions.text: Which ELF code and jurisdiction pair describes the organization's legal form, and which code-list version was used?
If no listed legal form applies, is the correct representation 8888 (pending listing) or 9999 (no separate legal form), and why?
answer_data: free-text legal form as stated locally

questions.text: Has the legal form changed through conversion, and what is the effective date of each form assignment?
Is the legal form valid only at a sub-national level requiring an ISO 3166-2 jurisdiction code?

data_elements.name: ELF code
data_elements.description: Four-character ISO 20275 entity legal form code.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction of legal formation
data_elements.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, or ISO 3166-2 subdivision code where the legal form exists only at subdivision level.

data_elements.name: Other legal form text
data_elements.description: Free-text legal form as stated locally, used when no listed ELF code applies.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The legal form assignment is a coded reference into an externally governed list; the authoritative artifact is the ELF code list itself, which is maintained upstream and referenced by version rather than copied, and the evidencing constitutive document is already held by the formation-act finding.

findings.name: Entity category, subcategory and legal personality
findings.description: LEI-CDF categorises entities as BRANCH, GENERAL, FUND, SOLE_PROPRIETOR, RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY or INTERNATIONAL_ORGANIZATION, with government subcategories. Category determines which other findings are even applicable and whether the subject has separate legal personality — a branch and a sole proprietorship do not.

questions.text: Which entity category and subcategory apply, and which facts of the record does that category make mandatory or inapplicable?
Does the organization have separate legal personality, and if not, which legal person bears its rights and obligations?
Is the organization unregistered or informal, such that registration, standing and succession findings do not apply?
answer_data: evidence of shared name and continuity

questions.text: Is this a government or international-organization subject whose formation rests on statute or treaty rather than registration?

data_elements.name: Entity category
data_elements.description: Coded category of the organization subject, controlling applicability of other findings.

data_elements.name: Separate legal personality flag
data_elements.description: Whether the organization is itself a legal person distinct from its members or parent.

data_elements.name: Formed by statute indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the organization was created by statute or treaty rather than by registration.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Category and personality are coded assertions evaluated against the constitutive act and register record; both evidencing artifacts already exist in the formation and registry-entry findings, and duplicating them here would split the evidence chain.

layers.name: Activity and statistical classification
layers.description: Coded economic-activity assignments under versioned schemes, and the organization's relationship to statistical units used by official registers.

findings.name: Activity code assignments across schemes
findings.description: Activity classification is scheme-bound and revision-bound: NACE Rev. 2.1 applies to European statistics from 2025 under Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/137, ISIC Rev. 5 was endorsed in 2023, and national registers use their own lists such as UK SIC. An assignment without its scheme version is not interpretable.

questions.text: Under which classification scheme and revision was each activity code assigned, and at which hierarchy level?
Which activity is the principal one, and by what criterion was principality determined?
answer_data: determination criterion (turnover, value added, headcount, self-declaration)

questions.text: Was the code assigned by the organization, by a register or by a statistical authority, and does that change its weight?
How are codes from a superseded revision carried forward, and is the mapping one-to-one?

data_elements.name: Activity code
data_elements.description: Code value assigned under a named classification scheme revision.

data_elements.name: Activity scheme version
data_elements.description: Identifier of the scheme and revision under which the code was assigned, mandatory whenever a code is present.

data_elements.name: Primary activity flag
data_elements.description: Whether this assignment represents the organization's principal activity.

artifacts.name: Activity scheme correspondence table
artifacts.description: Versioned crosswalk between activity schemes and revisions (NACE Rev. 2.1 to ISIC Rev. 5, national scheme to NACE, prior revision to current), recording mapping cardinality and ambiguity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite natural key of source scheme+revision and target scheme+revision as published by the maintaining statistical authority; each local release carries a version and an RFC 3339 publication timestamp.

findings.name: Statistical unit alignment
findings.description: Official registers hold enterprise group, enterprise and local unit as mandatory statistical units alongside legal units and their links, because an enterprise may span several legal units and group boundaries follow control rather than legal personality. Recording this alignment prevents an agent from silently merging legal units into one organization or splitting an organization to match a statistical unit.

questions.text: Which statistical unit types is this organization mapped to, and by which statistical authority?
answer_data: statistical unit type (legal unit, enterprise, enterprise group, local unit, kind-of-activity unit)

questions.text: Does the mapped enterprise span legal units other than this organization, and which ones?
Where is the group's global decision centre, and does it differ from this organization's jurisdiction?
Where the statistical view and the legal view disagree, which is authoritative for a given consumer?

data_elements.name: Statistical unit type
data_elements.description: Coded statistical unit to which this organization is mapped in an official business register.

data_elements.name: Statistical register reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the statistical business register and the unit identifier it assigns.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Statistical unit alignment is an assertion linking this record to units held in an external statistical register; the authoritative artifact is that register's own record, which is not redistributable in most jurisdictions, so only the reference and its provenance are retained.

layers.name: Declared purpose and scale
layers.description: What the organization states about its own mission, non-profit character and size, and how those self-declarations are dated and evidenced.

findings.name: Declared purpose, object clause and non-profit status
findings.description: W3C ORG models purpose as a first-class property and schema.org exposes nonprofitStatus and ownershipFundingInfo. Purpose statements are either constitutive (an object clause in the charter) or self-declared marketing text, and the two carry very different weight; non-profit status is a jurisdiction-granted determination, not a self-description.

questions.text: Is this purpose statement a constitutive object clause, a governing-body resolution or self-declared communication?
Which authority granted the non-profit, charitable or public-benefit status, under which instrument, and is it time-limited?
answer_data: grant date and expiry or review date

questions.text: Does the declared purpose legally restrict what the organization may do, and what is the consequence of acting outside it?
When was the purpose statement last reviewed or reaffirmed, and does it still match the registered object clause?

data_elements.name: Purpose statement text
data_elements.description: The declared mission or object clause text with its language tag.

data_elements.name: Non-profit status code
data_elements.description: Coded charitable, public-benefit or non-profit determination as granted in a named jurisdiction.

data_elements.name: Purpose declaration timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with offset recording when the purpose statement was declared or reaffirmed.

artifacts.name: Purpose declaration record
artifacts.description: Dated capture of a purpose or status declaration with its text, language, source class, granting instrument reference and retrieval metadata.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Where a granting authority issues a reference (ruling or registration number), that reference plus authority code is the key; otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension with the declaration timestamp held as an attribute, not as the key.

findings.name: Scale, workforce and size-class measures
findings.description: Size indicators such as headcount are measurements with a method, unit, reference period and source, not static attributes. schema.org exposes numberOfEmployees and statistical registers hold size variables; without a reference period and a counting basis (headcount, full-time equivalent, including or excluding contractors) the figure is not comparable.

questions.text: On what counting basis and for which reference period is each size figure stated?
Who produced the size figure — the organization, a register, or a third party — and is it audited?
Which size class does the figure place the organization in, under which jurisdiction's thresholds?
Does the figure cover this organization alone or a consolidated group, and which entities are included?

data_elements.name: Workforce count
data_elements.description: Numeric size figure with an explicit counting basis and unit.

data_elements.name: Measurement reference period
data_elements.description: The period the figure describes, distinct from when it was reported or ingested.

data_elements.name: Size class code
data_elements.description: Coded size band under a named jurisdictional threshold scheme.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Size measures are reported values whose evidencing documents (annual accounts, statistical returns) belong to reporting and financial models outside this scope; retaining a separate artifact here would duplicate filings already covered by the recurring-obligations finding.

bundles.name: Formation, registration standing and lifecycle
bundles.description: How the organization came into existence, where it is recorded, what its current standing is, what recurring obligations keep that standing alive, and how it changes or ends.
bundles.rationale: LEI-CDF separates EntityStatus from RegistrationStatus, proving that the subject's existence and the record's standing are independent state machines; Companies House adds a twelve-value national status enumeration plus status detail; W3C ORG models ChangeEvent with originalOrganization and resultedFrom for succession; and the EU BRIS regime requires a register-issued identifier for companies and branches. These are distinct, separately answerable concerns.

layers.name: Formation and registry entries
layers.description: The constitutive act that created the organization and the entries that public and private registers hold about it.

findings.name: Formation act and creation date
findings.description: LEI-CDF records EntityCreationDate as the legal establishment date, schema.org records foundingDate and foundingLocation, BODS records foundingDate and formedByStatute, and Companies House records date_of_creation. Formation date and first registration date are frequently different and must not be conflated.

questions.text: On what date did the organization legally come into existence, and is that the same as its first registration date?
Which instrument created the organization — articles, deed, statute, treaty or a founding resolution — and where is it held?
In which jurisdiction and at which location was the organization founded, and does that differ from its current jurisdiction?
If no formation date is known or the organization predates its register, how is that recorded without fabricating a date?

data_elements.name: Entity creation date
data_elements.description: Date on which the organization was legally established, with precision declared.

data_elements.name: Constitutive instrument reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the founding instrument held in the charter model or by a custodian.

data_elements.name: Founding jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction under whose law the organization was constituted.

artifacts.name: Formation evidence extract
artifacts.description: Captured evidence of the constitutive act: certificate of incorporation, registration confirmation, statutory instrument citation or founding minutes, with retrieval metadata and a content digest.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuing authority code plus the authority's own document or entry number where issued; otherwise a UUID assigned by the adopting Dimension. The document date is metadata and is never used as the identifier.

findings.name: Registry entry and registration authority
findings.description: An entry links the organization to an authoritative source through a register code plus a local entity number, as in LEI-CDF's RegistrationAuthorityID and RegistrationAuthorityEntityID, drawing on a governed list of more than 1,050 registers across 232 jurisdictions. The EU adds the EUID, which must be ISO 6523 compliant and unequivocally identify companies and branches across interconnected registers.

questions.text: Which register holds an entry for this organization, and what is its governed register code?
What entry or registration number does that register assign, and what is its syntax and check rule?
How many registers hold entries for this organization, and which is authoritative for which fact?
Does the entry describe a branch or a foreign company rather than a domestically constituted organization?

data_elements.name: Register code
data_elements.description: Governed code identifying the registration or validation authority.

data_elements.name: Register entity number
data_elements.description: The entity's identification number as maintained by that register.

data_elements.name: Register entry date
data_elements.description: Date on which the register accepted the entry.

data_elements.name: Cross-register identifier
data_elements.description: Interconnection identifier such as the EU EUID used to address the organization across interconnected registers.

artifacts.name: Registry extract
artifacts.description: A point-in-time extract of the organization's entry in a named register, retained with register code, extract timestamp, requesting agent, licence terms and a content digest.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Register code plus register entity number plus the extract's RFC 3339 retrieval timestamp as a compound key; where the register issues an extract reference or version tag such as an entity tag, that reference takes priority.

layers.name: Standing, status and recurring obligations
layers.description: The organization's current legal standing, the separate standing of each record about it, and the periodic acts required to keep both current.

findings.name: Entity status distinguished from record registration status
findings.description: LEI-CDF keeps EntityStatus (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, NULL — whether the entity is legally registered and operating) strictly separate from RegistrationStatus (PENDING_VALIDATION, ISSUED, DUPLICATE, LAPSED, RETIRED, ANNULLED, CANCELLED, TRANSFERRED, PENDING_TRANSFER, PENDING_ARCHIVAL — the standing of the record). Companies House adds a twelve-value national enumeration plus company_status_detail. Collapsing these into one status field destroys answerability.

questions.text: Is the organization itself currently in existence and operating, and on what date was that last established?
What is the standing of each record about the organization, separately from the organization's own status?
Where a status is qualified (for example administration, liquidation or struck-off pending), what is the qualifying detail and the governing procedure?
How does a national status value map onto the model's normalised status, and what is lost in the mapping?

data_elements.name: Entity status
data_elements.description: Whether the organization is legally in existence and operating, coded under a named enumeration.

data_elements.name: Record registration status
data_elements.description: Standing of a specific record or registration about the organization, coded under that scheme's enumeration.

data_elements.name: Status detail
data_elements.description: Qualifying detail for a status, such as the insolvency or dissolution procedure in progress.

data_elements.name: Status observation timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset recording when the status was observed, held separately from the status effective date.

artifacts.name: Status observation record
artifacts.description: Dated observation of a status value from a named source, carrying both the effective date asserted by the source and the observation timestamp, so that stale and conflicting statuses remain distinguishable.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Compound key of organization canonical key, status scheme and RFC 3339 observation timestamp; ULID fallback assigned by the adopting Dimension when the source provides no stable observation reference.

findings.name: Recurring filing and renewal obligations
findings.description: Standing is maintained by periodic acts: LEI records carry NextRenewalDate and lapse if not renewed, and national registers require confirmation statements and accounts with their own due dates. Missing a due date changes record standing without changing the organization's existence.

questions.text: Which recurring obligations apply to this organization, under which instrument, and at what frequency?
What is the next due date for each obligation, and what is the consequence of missing it?
What evidence shows an obligation was fulfilled, and where is that evidence retrievable?
Is the organization exempt from an otherwise applicable obligation, and on what recorded basis?

data_elements.name: Obligation type
data_elements.description: Coded recurring obligation such as record renewal, confirmation statement or annual accounts filing.

data_elements.name: Next due date
data_elements.description: Date by which the next fulfilment of the obligation is required.

data_elements.name: Last fulfilment reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the most recent filing or renewal that satisfied the obligation.

artifacts.name: Obligation schedule
artifacts.description: Derived but persisted schedule of applicable obligations with authority, frequency, due dates, grace periods, fulfilment references and consequence codes, used to drive monitoring.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Compound key of organization canonical key, obligation type code and obligation period; schedule revisions are versioned with RFC 3339 generation timestamps rather than being overwritten.

layers.name: Lifecycle events and succession
layers.description: Discrete events that change the organization or its record, and the lineage links that connect predecessor and successor organizations.

findings.name: Lifecycle event records
findings.description: LEI-CDF v3.1 introduced LegalEntityEvents as a container carrying event type, dates, validation documents and the fields affected. W3C ORG models ChangeEvent linked by changedBy and resultedFrom. An event record must separate the date the event legally took effect from the date it was recorded and the date it was observed.

questions.text: What type of lifecycle event occurred, and which fields of the organization record does it affect?
What are the event's effective date, its recorded date at the authority, and the observation time in this system?
Which validation documents evidence the event, and who validated them?
Is the event completed, in progress or withdrawn, and can it be superseded by a later correction?

data_elements.name: Lifecycle event type code
data_elements.description: Coded event type such as name change, legal form conversion, seat transfer, merger, division, dissolution or status change.

data_elements.name: Event effective date
data_elements.description: Date on which the event took legal effect, distinct from its recording and observation times.

data_elements.name: Event observation timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset recording when this system learned of the event.

data_elements.name: Affected fields
data_elements.description: List of record fields whose values the event changes.

artifacts.name: Lifecycle event journal
artifacts.description: Append-only journal of lifecycle events with type, three distinct timestamps, affected fields, validation document references, asserting agent and supersession links.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authority-issued event or filing reference where available (register code plus filing number); otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Journal entries are ordered by RFC 3339 observation timestamp and never rekeyed.

findings.name: Succession, continuity and lineage
findings.description: W3C ORG treats an organization resulting from a change event as sufficiently distinct to have its own identity, linked to originalOrganization; LEI-CDF carries SuccessorEntity with SuccessorLEI or SuccessorEntityName; Eurostat register practice defines continuity rules for unit births and deaths. The hard question is when a change preserves identity and when it creates a new subject.

questions.text: Did this change preserve the organization's identity, or did it terminate one subject and create another?
Which organizations are predecessors and which are successors, and what is the cardinality of the transition?
If a successor exists but has no identifier, how is it recorded without inventing one?
Which identifiers, registrations, obligations and relationships transfer to the successor and which lapse?

data_elements.name: Successor reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of a successor organization, or its name where no identifier exists.

data_elements.name: Predecessor reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of a predecessor organization from which this subject resulted.

data_elements.name: Continuity decision
data_elements.description: Coded determination of whether identity was preserved across the transition, with the rule applied.

artifacts.name: Lineage graph record
artifacts.description: Persisted predecessor/successor edge set with transition cardinality, effective dates, continuity decisions and the rule versions applied, enabling a lineage view without recomputation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Edges keyed by the pair of organization canonical keys plus the lifecycle event reference that created the edge; a dimension-assigned ULID is used only when the causing event has no authority reference.

bundles.name: Control, ownership and representation
bundles.description: External relationships that determine who controls the organization, who owns or benefits from it, and who may act for it.
bundles.rationale: RR-CDF defines a normative, period-bounded and quantified model of consolidation and fund relationships with explicit reporting exceptions; BODS defines a statement-based model of ownership and control interests with direct/indirect and share ranges; ISO 5009 supplies codes for official roles tied to legal forms and explicitly excludes internal functional titles. Together they establish that control, ownership and representation are three distinct relationship families with different evidence regimes.

layers.name: Group structure and ownership
layers.description: Consolidation and group membership links, and ownership or control interests including beneficial ownership.

findings.name: Consolidation, branch and fund relationship links
findings.description: RR-CDF records IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY, IS_ULTIMATELY_CONSOLIDATED_BY, IS_INTERNATIONAL_BRANCH_OF, IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY, IS_SUBFUND_OF and IS_FEEDER_TO, each with up to three distinct period types, a status, quantifiers with a measurement method, and eight exception reasons for when a parent cannot be reported.

questions.text: Which relationship type connects this organization to the other party, and in which direction?
Which distinct periods apply — relationship validity, accounting period and document filing period — and do they differ?
answer_data: document filing period start and end

questions.text: What quantified measure describes the relationship, and by which measurement method and unit?
If no parent can be reported, which exception reason applies and when will it be reviewed?

data_elements.name: Relationship type code
data_elements.description: Coded organization-to-organization relationship such as direct or ultimate consolidation, branch, fund management, sub-fund or feeder.

data_elements.name: Relationship period
data_elements.description: A typed interval qualifying the relationship, with the period type declared.

data_elements.name: Relationship quantifier
data_elements.description: Quantified measure of the relationship with its measurement method and unit.

data_elements.name: Reporting exception reason
data_elements.description: Coded reason a required parent relationship is not reported.

artifacts.name: Organization relationship record
artifacts.description: A standalone relationship record carrying both endpoints, type, typed periods, status, quantifiers, validation sources and documents, and its own registration metadata — modelled separately from either endpoint's record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Compound natural key of start node identifier, end node identifier and relationship type, versioned by RFC 3339 last-update timestamp; where the issuing organization assigns a relationship reference, that reference takes priority.

findings.name: Ownership and beneficial-ownership interests
findings.description: BODS models ownership and control as relationship records with a subject entity, an interested party, and an array of interests each carrying type, directOrIndirect, a beneficialOwnershipOrControl flag valid only for natural persons, share values expressible as exact figures or as minimum/maximum ranges, and start and end dates. Indirect chains are represented through component records rather than collapsed edges.

questions.text: What type of interest does the interested party hold, in what amount or range, and is it held directly or indirectly?
answer_data: share exact value or minimum and maximum bounds

questions.text: Is this interest asserted as beneficial ownership or control by a natural person, and under which jurisdiction's threshold?
Where the interested party is unknown or unspecified, what reason is recorded and what is the follow-up?
For an indirect interest, which component records describe each step of the ownership chain?
Who asserted this ownership statement, on what date, from which source type, and under what licence is it published?
answer_data: source type (self-declaration, official register, third party, verified)

data_elements.name: Interest type
data_elements.description: Coded kind of ownership or control interest, such as shareholding, voting rights or right to appoint directors.

data_elements.name: Interest share
data_elements.description: Share of the interest expressed as an exact percentage or as a bounded range with inclusive or exclusive limits.

data_elements.name: Interested party reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the person or organization holding the interest, or an explicit unspecified-party marker.

data_elements.name: Statement date
data_elements.description: Date or RFC 3339 date-time at which the ownership statement was made, distinct from the interest start date.

artifacts.name: Ownership statement set
artifacts.description: A published set of ownership and control statements about the organization, carrying publication details (publication date, standard version, licence, publisher) and per-statement source metadata including retrieval time and asserting party.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Statement identifiers assigned by the publisher, recommended as ULIDs, retained verbatim; the set is keyed by publisher identifier plus publication date, and statements are never re-keyed on ingestion.

layers.name: Official roles, representation and affiliation
layers.description: Who is empowered to act for the organization under law, and which external bodies the organization is affiliated with or accredited by.

findings.name: Official organizational roles and authorised representation
findings.description: ISO 5009 codes cover over 2,000 official roles across almost 250 legal forms in 89 jurisdictions, are tied to the relevant ELF code, include only roles appearing in local legislation, and explicitly exclude internal functional titles such as Chief Risk Officer. W3C ORG separates Role, Post and Membership. This finding covers the organization-side view: which posts exist and what they authorise, not the persons filling them.

questions.text: Which official organizational roles exist for this organization's legal form, and what are their governed codes?
What may a holder of each role bind the organization to, and are there joint-signature or threshold constraints?
Is the appointment currently in force, and what are its start and end dates as recorded by the authority?
Is a claimed title an official role under local legislation or an internal functional title with no statutory effect?

data_elements.name: Official organizational role code
data_elements.description: Six-character governed code for an official role, valid in combination with a legal form and jurisdiction.

data_elements.name: Representation power
data_elements.description: Description of what a role holder may bind the organization to, including joint-signature rules.

data_elements.name: Appointment interval
data_elements.description: Start and end of an appointment to an official role, as recorded by the competent authority.

artifacts.name: Representation authority record
artifacts.description: Record of who may represent the organization, linking an official role code, the appointed party reference held in the person model, the authorising instrument and the appointment interval, with personal data minimised to a reference.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authority-issued appointment or officer reference plus register code where available; otherwise a UUID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Person names are never used as keys.

findings.name: External affiliation, membership and accreditation
findings.description: Organizations belong to federations, chambers, standards bodies and networks, and hold accreditations or certifications granted by external bodies. W3C ORG models Membership as an n-ary relation between agent, organization and role; schema.org exposes memberOf and hasCredential. These links are neither ownership nor control and must not be conflated with them.

questions.text: Which external body is the organization affiliated with or accredited by, and what is that body's own identifier?
What rights, obligations or claims does the affiliation confer, and is it publicly verifiable?
Over which period is the affiliation or accreditation valid, and what triggers its lapse or withdrawal?
Is this link genuinely non-controlling, or does it in substance confer control that belongs in the ownership layer?

data_elements.name: Affiliation type
data_elements.description: Coded kind of external link such as association membership, accreditation, certification or network participation.

data_elements.name: Affiliating body reference
data_elements.description: Scheme-qualified identifier of the external body conferring the affiliation.

data_elements.name: Affiliation validity interval
data_elements.description: Period over which the affiliation or accreditation is valid.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Affiliation and accreditation evidence is issued and published by the conferring body, which is a separate organization subject; this model retains only the scheme-qualified link, validity and verification endpoint, because copying certificates would create an unmaintained duplicate of another party's authoritative record.

bundles.name: Presence and reachability
bundles.description: Where the organization is legally seated, where it actually operates, and through which electronic addresses and channels it can be reached.
bundles.rationale: LEI-CDF distinguishes LegalAddress from HeadquartersAddress and OtherAddresses with transliterated variants; W3C ORG separates hasRegisteredSite from hasSite; Companies House exposes registered_office_is_in_dispute and undeliverable_registered_office_address, proving that a registered address is a legal construct that can be contested or non-functional; and Peppol shows that electronic addressing uses the same scheme-qualified pattern as identity.

layers.name: Locations, sites and channels
layers.description: Registered and operating locations of the organization together with its electronic addresses and public channels, each with a role, validity and reachability status.

findings.name: Registered office and legal address
findings.description: The registered office is the address at which the organization is legally addressable in its jurisdiction of formation; it is frequently not an operating location and may be a service-provider address. National registers record when it is in dispute or undeliverable, which are distinct states from being absent.

questions.text: Which address is the registered or legal address, as distinct from the headquarters and other addresses?
Is the registered address disputed, undeliverable or served by a third-party provider, and since when?
When did the registered address last change, and which lifecycle event and filing recorded the change?
In which language and script is the address authoritative, and is a transliterated form required for interchange?

data_elements.name: Address role
data_elements.description: Coded role of an address such as legal/registered, headquarters, service or other.

data_elements.name: Structured address
data_elements.description: Address components with country and subdivision codes, retained in the source language and script.

data_elements.name: Address condition flag
data_elements.description: Coded condition such as in dispute, undeliverable or provider-served.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Registered address values are carried inline on the organization record and evidenced by the registry extract artifact already retained by the registry-entry finding; geometry, building identity and postal normalisation belong to the referenced place model rather than to a duplicated artifact here.

findings.name: Operating sites, branches and service areas
findings.description: W3C ORG models Site as a place where an organization operates and separates hasSite from hasRegisteredSite. Operating presence is distinct from legal seat: a branch may be separately registered and separately identified, while a site may be purely operational with no registry footprint at all.

questions.text: What kind of presence is this — registered branch, operating site, local unit or service point — and is it separately registered?
Over which period was the site active, and what evidences its opening and closing?
Which geographic areas does the organization serve from this site, and at what granularity is that recorded?
Which place or facility record does this site resolve to, and who maintains that record?

data_elements.name: Site kind
data_elements.description: Coded kind of operating presence.

data_elements.name: Site place reference
data_elements.description: Reference into the place or facility model where the site's spatial detail is held.

data_elements.name: Served area
data_elements.description: Coded geographic area served, at a declared granularity.

artifacts.name: Organization site register
artifacts.description: Maintained list of the organization's sites and branches with kind, place reference, separate-registration status, validity interval and evidence references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Branch registration number plus register code where the site is separately registered; otherwise a UUID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Addresses are never used as site keys because they are not unique or stable.

findings.name: Electronic addresses and public channels
findings.description: Electronic business addressing uses the same scheme-qualified pattern as identity: a Peppol participant is addressed as an ISO 6523 scheme designator plus a value, for example 0199 with an LEI or 0208 with a Belgian enterprise number. Public channels such as websites and published contact points are separate, weaker assertions that require their own verification.

questions.text: Under which electronic addressing scheme is the organization reachable, and what is the scheme-qualified address?
How was each channel verified as belonging to this organization, and when?
What is each channel authorised for — legal service, invoicing, general enquiry or public communication?
Which channels are retired, and are prior references redirected or tombstoned?

data_elements.name: Electronic address scheme
data_elements.description: Governed designator of the electronic addressing scheme, such as an ISO 6523 ICD code used in a business network.

data_elements.name: Electronic address value
data_elements.description: The address value under the named scheme.

data_elements.name: Public channel URI
data_elements.description: URI of a public channel such as a website or published contact endpoint.

data_elements.name: Channel verification timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset for the most recent channel verification.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Electronic addresses are scheme-qualified inline values whose authoritative artifact is the network's own participant registry, queried by resolution rather than copied; retaining a local artifact would produce stale routing data with no way to detect divergence.

bundles.name: Record governance and interoperability
bundles.description: Governance of the organization record itself: where each assertion came from, how well corroborated it is, who may see it, how long it is kept, and how it maps onto external standards.
bundles.rationale: LEI-CDF records ValidationSources with graded corroboration levels and a ValidationAuthority, PROV-O supplies the normative vocabulary for attributing assertions to agents and deriving records from sources, BODS requires per-statement source and publication metadata including licence, and national registers expose concurrency and completeness markers. Standard alignment must be recorded as mapping with declared loss, not as conformance.

layers.name: Provenance, quality, access and retention
layers.description: Per-assertion provenance and corroboration, data-quality assessment, disclosure classification and retention rules for the organization record.

findings.name: Assertion provenance and attribution
findings.description: Every field value is an assertion by some agent from some source at some time. PROV-O supplies wasAttributedTo, wasDerivedFrom, wasGeneratedBy and actedOnBehalfOf with prov:Organization as an agent type; BODS requires source type, url, retrievedAt and assertedBy on each statement. Event time and observation time must be recorded separately.

questions.text: From which source was each assertion derived, of what source type, and under what licence may it be reused?
answer_data: source type (official register, self-declaration, third party, verified)

questions.text: Which agent asserted the value, and on whose behalf were they acting?
Was the value copied, transformed or inferred, and from which prior version was it derived?
Are event time and observation/ingestion time recorded separately for this assertion, and with what precision?

data_elements.name: Assertion source reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and URL of the source from which an assertion was taken, with its source type.

data_elements.name: Asserting agent
data_elements.description: Agent that made the assertion, typed as person, organization or software agent.

data_elements.name: Retrieval timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset recording when the source was retrieved, distinct from any date asserted by the source.

artifacts.name: Record provenance graph
artifacts.description: Graph of entities, activities and agents describing how each version of the organization record was generated, derived and attributed, using qualified provenance where circumstances matter.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each provenance node keyed by a dereferenceable IRI within the adopting Dimension namespace; activity nodes carry RFC 3339 start and end times as attributes and are never keyed by time.

findings.name: Validation, corroboration level and data quality
findings.description: LEI-CDF grades a record's corroboration as PENDING, ENTITY_SUPPLIED_ONLY, PARTIALLY_CORROBORATED or FULLY_CORROBORATED against a named ValidationAuthority, and RR-CDF carries validation sources, documents and references. Companies House marks partial_data_available and exposes an entity tag for concurrency. Quality is therefore a declared, evidenced grade rather than an assumed property.

questions.text: What corroboration level applies to this record, and against which validation authority and documents was it established?
How stale is each value relative to its source's own update cadence, and when must it be refreshed?
Which required fields are absent or only partially available, and is that a source limitation or an ingestion gap?
What version or entity tag did the source return, and how are lost updates prevented on write-back?

data_elements.name: Corroboration level
data_elements.description: Graded level of corroboration of the record against authoritative sources.

data_elements.name: Validation authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the authority whose source was used to corroborate the record.

data_elements.name: Record version tag
data_elements.description: Opaque version or entity tag used for optimistic concurrency against a source or consumer.

data_elements.name: Last update timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset for the most recent change to the record.

artifacts.name: Data quality assessment
artifacts.description: Periodic assessment of the organization record against declared quality criteria, recording corroboration level, completeness, staleness, detected conflicts and remediation actions with owners and due dates.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Compound key of organization canonical key and assessment period identifier, with a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension per assessment run; the run timestamp is an attribute, not the key.

findings.name: Disclosure classification, access and retention
findings.description: Organization records mix data that registers publish freely, data that is licensed, and data that identifies natural persons and therefore carries privacy obligations. BODS requires an explicit licence on publication; national registers operate protected-address and secure-officer regimes; and retention must be decided per class rather than for the record as a whole.

questions.text: What disclosure class does each field group carry — publicly disclosed, licensed, restricted or personal-data-bearing?
Under which licence was source data obtained, and does that licence permit redistribution in the intended projection?
Which fields identify natural persons, and what minimisation is applied before the record is shared?
How long is each class retained, what triggers deletion or archival, and what survives as a tombstone?
How can the organization or a data subject request correction or erasure, and how is the outcome evidenced?

data_elements.name: Disclosure class
data_elements.description: Coded disclosure classification applied to a field group of the organization record.

data_elements.name: Source licence URI
data_elements.description: URI of the licence under which source data was obtained and may be redistributed.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Retention duration applicable to a disclosure class, with its triggering event.

data_elements.name: Suppression flag
data_elements.description: Indicator that a value is suppressed or protected under an authority's protection regime.

artifacts.name: Disclosure and retention policy record
artifacts.description: Versioned policy mapping each field group of the organization record to a disclosure class, licence constraint, minimisation rule, retention period, deletion trigger and tombstone specification.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Policy identifier within the adopting Dimension namespace plus a monotonically increasing version; effective-from and effective-to are RFC 3339 attributes and superseded versions are retained, not overwritten.

layers.name: Interoperability and mapping
layers.description: Declared alignments to external standards and the recorded divergences between sources that assert different values for the same organization.

findings.name: Standard alignment, crosswalks and register divergence
findings.description: External standards are alignments, not conformance claims. W3C ORG, schema.org, LEI-CDF, NACE and ISIC each cover overlapping but non-identical ground, and national registers legitimately disagree with global ones about name, status and address. Divergence must be recorded as an observation with sources, not silently resolved.

questions.text: To which external standard, version and element does each model element map, and is the mapping exact, broader, narrower or partial?
Is a conformance claim being made, and if so what evidence supports it, or is this alignment only?
Where two sources assert different values for the same fact, what is recorded and which source prevails for which consumer?
Which projections are published from this model, and which fields does each deliberately omit?

data_elements.name: Alignment mapping
data_elements.description: Mapping from a model element to an external standard element with the mapping relation and declared loss.

data_elements.name: Conflict observation
data_elements.description: Recorded disagreement between sources about a fact, with values, sources and observation time.

data_elements.name: Precedence rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the rule determining which source prevails for a given fact and consumer.

artifacts.name: Alignment and conflict register
artifacts.description: Versioned register of external-standard mappings with relation types and declared losses, together with an append-only log of observed inter-source conflicts, precedence decisions and their rationale.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Mappings keyed by source element identifier plus target standard, version and element identifier; conflict entries keyed by a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension and ordered by RFC 3339 observation timestamp.

functions.name: Resolve organization identifier
functions.description: Resolve a scheme-qualified identifier to the canonical organization record, returning a minimal profile and the corroboration level of the answer.
outputs: minimal profile fields for the requested projection
preconditions: The scheme designator exists in the identifier scheme catalogue
The requesting agent holds access to the requested projection
The identifier passes the scheme's syntax and check-character rule
effects: Emits a resolution audit entry with agent, scheme, value and timestamp
Records a negative-resolution entry when no record matches, to avoid repeated lookups

functions.name: Ingest registry extract
functions.description: Ingest a point-in-time extract from a named register, storing it as an immutable artifact and deriving field-level assertions with provenance.
preconditions: The register code exists in the governed registration-authority list
The extract carries or is assigned a content digest
The licence permits the intended storage and projection
effects: Creates an immutable extract artifact with digest and retrieval metadata
Appends provenance nodes attributing each derived assertion to the register
Raises conflict observations where derived values disagree with held values

functions.name: Assert lifecycle event
functions.description: Record a lifecycle event affecting the organization, with separate effective, authority-recording and observation times, affected fields and validation documents.
preconditions: The event type exists in the governed event type list
The asserting agent is authorised to assert events for this organization
Effective date is not later than the observation timestamp unless a future-dated filing is explicitly flagged
effects: Appends an entry to the append-only lifecycle event journal
Updates affected fields and retains the prior values as a versioned snapshot
Triggers re-evaluation of standing and obligation schedules

functions.name: Evaluate succession continuity
functions.description: Decide whether a transition preserved organizational identity or created a new subject, and write the resulting lineage edges.
preconditions: The transition event exists in the lifecycle journal
A continuity rule set version is declared and retrievable
At least one predecessor is identified by a canonical key
effects: Writes lineage edges keyed by predecessor, successor and causing event
Marks identifiers as carried over or lapsed on the affected records
Records the decision, deciding agent and rule version in the resolution decision log

functions.name: Reconcile duplicate organization records
functions.description: Compare candidate records, record the comparison evidence and confidence, and execute a merge, split or explicit non-match decision with a reversible tombstone.
preconditions: All candidates are readable by the deciding agent
Upstream duplicate or annulled status has been checked
A rollback path exists for the chosen action
effects: Writes an entry to the entity resolution decision log with evidence and confidence
Creates tombstones that keep retired keys resolvable to the survivor
Records explicit non-matches so the comparison is not repeated

functions.name: Assign or migrate activity classification
functions.description: Assign an activity code under a named scheme revision, or migrate an existing assignment to a newer revision using a published correspondence table.
outputs: activity code assignment with scheme version
preconditions: The target scheme revision is available in the local reference set
A correspondence table exists for the requested migration
The principality criterion is declared
effects: Writes the assignment with an explicit scheme revision
Retains the prior assignment with its revision rather than overwriting it
Flags migrations whose mapping is not one-to-one for review

functions.name: Record control or ownership relationship
functions.description: Create or update a relationship record between the organization and another party, with typed periods, quantifiers, interests and, where applicable, a reporting exception.
outputs: exception reason where no counterparty can be reported
preconditions: Both endpoints resolve, or the counterparty is explicitly marked unspecified with a reason
The relationship or interest type exists in the governed list
Beneficial-ownership flags are set only where the interested party is a natural person
effects: Writes a standalone relationship record with its own registration metadata
Records the source type, retrieval time and asserting party per statement
Records an exception reason and review date instead of omitting an unreportable link

functions.name: Evaluate record standing and obligations
functions.description: Recompute entity status, record registration status and the obligation schedule from held observations, flagging staleness and imminent lapse.
outputs: obligation schedule with next due dates
preconditions: At least one dated status observation exists
Obligation definitions carry authority, frequency and consequence
Status mapping tables are versioned and available
effects: Persists a status observation record rather than overwriting prior statuses
Regenerates the obligation schedule as a new version
Emits warnings where a value is older than its source's update cadence

functions.name: Publish governed projection
functions.description: Emit a scoped projection of the organization record — public directory card, compliance profile, lineage view or ownership disclosure — applying disclosure classification, minimisation and licence constraints.
preconditions: The projection is defined in the disclosure and retention policy
Source licences permit redistribution of every included field
Personal-data minimisation rules have been applied
effects: Records a disclosure event with audience, projection, policy version and timestamp
Suppresses fields carrying protection flags or incompatible licences
Attaches attribution and licence notices required by upstream sources

functions.name: Apply retention or erasure action
functions.description: Execute the retention decision for a field group or record: archive, delete, or minimise to a tombstone, with evidence of the action.
preconditions: The retention trigger has occurred and is evidenced
A statutory minimum retention period, where one applies, has elapsed
The authorising agent holds the retention authority for the scope
effects: Removes or archives the in-scope data and writes an irreversible action evidence record
Preserves a tombstone sufficient to keep prior references resolvable
